Sara — great meeting and thanks for the clear asks. I’m looping in Camila (solutions) and Aditya (SRE/product) to help with details. High-level summary below, and I’ve attached a draft SLO comparison matrix and a failover/test plan PDF for your review.

TL;DR summary vs hyperscalers:
- Uptime/SLA: Redwood offers a 99.95% SLA on Dedicated and 99.9% on Hosted API (we can discuss upgrade paths for contractual SLAs). Hyperscalers publish similar figures but the practical difference is in controlled fallbacks and predictable error budgets when models are served at scale.
- Rate limits & concurrency: Redwood exposes per-API-key concurrency controls and customer-configurable rate policies; hyperscalers typically have service-level quotas that are slower to adjust and can result in throttling without graceful circuit-breakers.
- Failover behavior: Redwood supports automatic routing to regional model replicas + automatic fallback to compatible model variants; our routing policy includes graceful degradation (lower-cost model variant with same interface) rather than immediate hard failures. Hyperscaler fallback usually requires manual multi-region endpoint configuration or custom logic.
- Observability & debugging: Redwood Console provides per-request traces, token-level latency breakdowns, and error budget alerts tied to your test prompt sets (this is often manual in hyperscaler flows).

Suggested next tests (we can run these from Redwood-managed harness or provide scripts for FinApps infra):
A) Sustained load: maintain 200 QPS for 30m, then ramp to 2k QPS for 10m; measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token error rates, and dropped requests.
B) Burst & token-rate limit edge: 10k requests in <1m to test throttling and graceful queueing behavior.
C) Region failover: kill primary region (simulated) and measure failover time to replica + request error spike and success rate during replication switch.
D) Error-budget burn: inject transient errors (5% -> 15%) and validate alerting, auto-throttle, and rollback behavior.

I've attached: slo_comparison_table.xlsx (tabbed by SLA, retry, rate limits, fallback behavior) and redwood_failover_test_plan.pdf (step-by-step test harness + expected pass/fail gates).

Action items / owners:
- Redwood: run A & B from our hosted harness and share raw traces (Aditya) — target Wed 18 Feb.
- FinApps: confirm a dedicated test window and whether you want us to run tests from US-west only or multi-region (Sara).
- Procurement: we'll include a one-page procurement readiness doc if you want formal SLAs added to the MSA (Marcus).

Camila/Aditya — can you confirm resource availability for Wed?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
